reasoning: Xi Jinping has consolidated supreme power, removed term limits, and faces no visible internal threats. Removal within 18 months would require an extraordinary event like a coup, severe health crisis, or massive unrest — all tail risks. A 7% probability significantly overstates the chance of such a black swan.
evidence_points: Xi eliminated presidential term limits in 2018, signaling indefinite rule.
No organized opposition exists within the CCP; key rivals purged.
The next Party Congress (2027) is beyond the market window, and Xi would normally transition then only if he chose.
sources_consulted: Analysis of Xi's anti-corruption campaign and power consolidation
Recent reporting on CCP internal dynamics
